judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Theme/Sub-Theme 'Basic Operations'. The first requires multiplying whole numbers from 1x1 to 9x9 (multiplication facts/times tables); the second requires dividing whole numbers not exceeding 48 by 2-6 without remainder. Division without remainder in this range is the inverse of the multiplication facts covered in the first objective, so fluency with those multiplication facts substantively supports success in this division work. This is a justified developmental dependency, not just shared hierarchy or generic token overlap (shared tokens 'whole','numbers' plus stopwords). Same Grade rank; direction is supported by the multiplication-to-division inverse relationship.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives dealing with fractions: the first is writing fractions of equivalent value (equivalent fractions under Theme NUMBER AND NUMERATION > Fraction), the second is subtracting fractions with the same denominator (under Theme BASIC OPERATIONS > Subtraction). They share genuine conceptual coherence around fraction concepts and reinforce fraction fluency, but sit in different themes/topics at the same canonical rank (Primary Three) with no clear developmental dependency: equivalent-fraction naming is not a prerequisite for same-denominator subtraction, and same-denominator subtraction does not build toward writing equivalent fractions. The token overlap is largely generic stem wording ('pupils','should','be','able','the','to') plus the shared 'fractions' term, which supports coherence but not a directional buildsTowards. relatesTo is the best-supported symmetric judgment.

Both are Primary Three (rank 2) performance objectives that apply multiplication in real-world/practical contexts, giving substantive conceptual coherence and mutually reinforcing application of the same skill. This supports symmetric relatesTo rather than a directional buildsTowards or no_relation.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic (2. Length). The first objective is measuring the length and/or width of objects; the second is finding perimeters of regular figures 'in metres and centimeters by measurement.' Perimeter-by-measurement directly requires the ability to measure lengths of edges, so proficiency in measuring length substantively supports success in finding perimeters. Same grade rank (PRIMARY THREE), but the conceptual dependency justifies a developmental direction from length measurement to perimeter measurement rather than mere co-topic relatedness.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives under Topic 2 Fractions (same Grade rank 1), so direction rests on substantive content, not hierarchy. The first objective—dividing a collection of concrete objects into two and four equal parts (halves and quarters, per its LCs)—establishes the partitioning-into-quarters skill that the second objective, 'obtain ¾ of a concrete object,' directly depends on: identifying three of four equal parts presupposes the ability to divide into four equal parts. Proficiency in the first therefore supports success in the second, justifying buildsTowards first_to_second. Shared tokens/quarters/fractions and page proximity are corroborating but not the basis of the decision.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives under Topic 2 Fractions (same Grade rank 1), so direction rests on substantive content, not hierarchy. Shared tokens/quarters/fractions and page proximity are corroborating but not the basis of the decision.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same 'Subtraction' Topic within the 'Basic Operations' Theme. The second (PRIMARY ONE) is 'crosscheck accuracy in subtraction' — a computation-verification skill; the first (PRIMARY TWO) is 'apply addition and subtraction in everyday activities' — a broader application objective. They share substantive subtraction coherence, but the specific skills differ (verification vs. real-world application) and no clear developmental dependency is established: accurate crosschecking is not a demonstrated prerequisite for everyday application. The overlap evidence is dominated by generic tokens ('able','be','pupils','should','to') plus the shared domain word 'subtraction', so a permitted developmental buildsTowards is not strongly warranted. Meaningful topic-level reinforcement supports symmetric relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY THREE Performance Objectives (rank 2, same grade) within the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) and Sub-Theme (Primary Measures), addressing measurement of length: the first mentions the importance/benefits of standard units of measurement (Topic '2. Length'), and the second identifies the differences in non-standard measures (Topic '3. Length II'). They share substantive conceptual coherence around understanding standard vs non-standard measures of length, meaningfully reinforcing each other. However, no clear developmental dependency direction is supported at the same grade rank—non-standard measure work and standard-unit rationale are complementary aspects rather than one clearly enabling the other—so relatesTo is the appropriate symmetric judgment. Lexical/hierarchy overlap alone was not treated as sufficient.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Basic Operations theme: 'subtract 3-digit numbers' (Topic: Subtraction) and 'multiply 2-digit number by 1-digit number' (Topic: Multiplication). They are complementary multi-digit whole-number computation skills that reinforce each other within the same basic-operations strand, but they are distinct operations with no directional dependency—subtraction proficiency does not specifically support multiplication success, and both sit at the same grade rank (rank 2, PRIMARY THREE), so no lower-to-higher developmental direction is warranted. The shared 'digit' token and page/rank proximity are generic and support consideration only. Substantive conceptual coherence as complementary arithmetic operations supports relatesTo.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives (rank gap 0) that apply addition to real-world contexts: the first is applying addition and subtraction to shop effectively with money not greater than ₦20 (Topic Money, Primary Measures), and the second is appreciating/mentioning the need for correct addition of numbers and fractions in everyday activities (Topic Addition, Basic Operations). They sit in different themes/sub-themes/topics and share the concept of addition used in everyday life, giving substantive conceptual coherence beyond the boilerplate 'pupils should be able to' token overlap. There is no clear developmental dependency at the same grade—one being an application skill and the other an affective appreciation—so a directed buildsTowards is not supported, while the complementary real-life addition focus supports relatesTo.
